sense: the historic centre of a city

terms.gloss: the old town, the first town round which a city grew
evidence: Varr. LL 6.34: lūstrātur antīquum oppidum Palātīnum
terms.comment: Varro’s phrase for the first town on the Palatine, the core of Rome; Varro also has antīqua urbs for it. Antīquus is what belongs to former times, so it suits an old quarter that was once the whole town.

phrases.latin: Per antīquum oppidum ad castellum ascendēmus.
phrases.english: We’ll go up through the old town to the castle.

phrases.latin: Lupercīs nūdīs lūstrātur antīquum oppidum Palātīnum gregibus hūmānīs cīnctum
phrases.english: the old town on the Palatine is purified by the naked Luperci, and ringed with crowds of people

phrases.latin: Subūram Jūnius scrībit ab eō, quod fuerit sub antīquā urbe
phrases.english: Junius writes that the Subura is named from its lying below the old city

sources: Lewis & Short: antiquus · Lewis & Short: oppidum
